literature_notes: HCN4 has an intracellular N-terminus (residues 1–262) and an intracellular C-terminus (residues 512–1203); its only extracellular-facing spans are the short S1–S2 loop (288–295, 8 aa), S3–S4 loop (360–375, 16 aa), and the S5–pore–S6 turret (429–491, 63 aa). L1, L2, and L3 all report eGFP or twin-strep tags fused to the N-terminus of full-length HCN4 constructs; because the N-terminus is cytoplasmic, these are intracellular tags and do not qualify as extracellular surface sites — they are recorded in other_positions. L4, L5, and L6 describe an E. coli autotransporter surface-display system in which the isolated HCN4 C-Linker-CNBD passenger domain (a soluble fragment, not full-length membrane-anchored protein) is fused to the EhaA translocator; the Myc-tag resides on the EhaA-Linker component, not within HCN4 itself. This construct is equivalent to a secreted ectodomain reagent and is explicitly excluded by the evidence rules. No ledger line grounds a tag insertion at an extracellular position of full-length, membrane-anchored HCN4; zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: eGFP fused immediately before residue 1 (N-terminal prepend) of full-length HCN4; the N-terminus lies in the intracellular span 1–262, so this is a cytoplasmic tag — tolerated and used for MACS/FACS cell sorting, but not a surface-exposed site.
N-terminal eGFP (followed by 3C protease site) on full-length hHCN4 (Δ782–1062 truncation); same intracellular N-terminus as L1 — cytoplasmic tag, not extracellular.
Twin-strep tag prepended to the N-terminus of the GFP-hHCN4Δ282C construct for affinity purification; N-terminus is intracellular, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
